title: Flatness and finite presentation of algebras over a ring fibre product
statement:
Let $A',A,B$ be commutative rings with identity, let $q:A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ be surjective, and let $B\to A$ be a ring map. Put $I=\ker q$ and $R=B\times_A A'=\{(b,a'):b|_A=q(a')\}$, with coordinatewise ring operations. Let $D$ be a commutative $B$-algebra, $C'$ a commutative $A'$-algebra, and $\varphi:D\otimes_B A\xrightarrow{\sim}C'/IC'$ an $A$-algebra isomorphism. Put $C=C'/IC'$ and $E=D\times_C C'$, where $D\to C$ is $d\mapsto\varphi(d\otimes1)$. The canonical maps give $E$ its $R$-algebra structure. Then $R\to E$ is flat if and only if $B\to D$ and $A'\to C'$ are flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Moreover $R\to E$ is flat and of finite presentation if and only if both $B\to D$ and $A'\to C'$ are flat and of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. For every flat commutative $R$-algebra $L$, the canonical ring homomorphism
$$L\longrightarrow(L\otimes_R B)\times_{L\otimes_R A}(L\otimes_R A')$$
is an isomorphism. Zero rings are allowed, and no nilpotence, finite generation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $I$.

source.place: Tag 08KQ, lemma-properties-algebras-over-fibre-product, parts (2), (3) and the final assertion, in Situation 08KH (situation-module-over-fibre-product).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-patched-module-base-change] to the underlying compatible modules $D,C'$. It gives the canonical isomorphisms $E\otimes_R B\simeq D$ and $E\otimes_R A'\simeq C'$. These are algebra isomorphisms: the maps send $(d,c')\otimes b$ to $bd$ and $(d,c')\otimes a'$ to $a'c'$, respectively, so preserve products and units. Thus they identify the actual structural ring maps, without a flatness assumption.

source.place: Tag 08KQ, proof opening paragraph; Tag 07RU, canonical base-change maps

proof.text: If $E$ is flat over $R$, the two scalar extensions in step 1 are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change]. If $E$ is also finitely presented as an $R$-algebra, they are finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition](1). This proves the forward directions of both equivalences.

source.place: Tag 08KQ, proof opening paragraph, forward implications

proof.text: Conversely, if $D$ is flat over $B$ and $C'$ over $A'$, apply [lem-sfb-flat-module-fibre-product-patching] to their underlying modules. It makes $E$ flat over $R$. For a flat $R$-algebra $L$, the second assertion of that same module lemma makes the displayed canonical map for $L$ bijective. This map preserves multiplication and the unit since its two components are $l\mapsto l\otimes1$; a bijective ring homomorphism is a ring isomorphism. This proves the flatness equivalence and the final assertion for arbitrary flat $L$.

source.place: Tag 08KQ, proof Ad (2) and final assertion; Tag 0D2I, parts (1), (2)

proof.text: Assume now that $D/B$ and $C'/A'$ are flat and finitely presented. Their finite polynomial presentations supply finite algebra generators $x_i$ of $D$ and $y_j$ of $C'$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. The projection $E\to D$ is surjective because $C'\to C$ is, so choose lifts $u_i\in E$ of $x_i$. The canonical surjection $E\otimes_R A'\to C'$ in step 1 expresses the finitely many $y_j$ as finite sums $\sum_k a'_{jk}\overline v_k$ for a finite list $v_k\in E$. Consequently the images of this list generate $C'$ as an $A'$-algebra. Combining the $u_i,v_k$ gives a list $e_1,\ldots,e_n\in E$ whose images generate $D/B$ and $C'/A'$. Put $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ and evaluate $t_i\mapsto e_i$.

Write $P_B=B[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, $P_{A'}=A'[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, $P_A=A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. Coefficientwise, $P=P_B\times_{P_A}P_{A'}$ and $P_{A'}\to P_A$ is surjective. Evaluation gives surjections $P_B\to D$ and $P_{A'}\to C'$, so these are cyclic, hence finite, modules over the indicated polynomial rings. Their reductions over $P_A$ identify with $C$: in $D\otimes_{P_B}P_A$ each variable acts as the prescribed image of $e_i$, leaving precisely $D\otimes_B A$, and likewise $C'\otimes_{P_{A'}}P_A=C'/IC'$. The given $\varphi$ respects these variable actions because $e_i\in E$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-module-fibre-product-patching] to this polynomial-ring square and these modules. It says that $E$ is finite as a $P$-module. If $w_1,\ldots,w_m$ generate that module, then $e_1,\ldots,e_n,w_1,\ldots,w_m$ generate $E$ as an $R$-algebra: every element is a sum $\sum_j f_j(e_1,\ldots,e_n)w_j$. Enlarge the list $e_i$ by these $w_j$ and reset $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. Evaluation $P\twoheadrightarrow E$ is now surjective, and both evaluated scalar extensions remain surjective.

source.place: Tag 08KQ, proof Ad (1), polynomial cube and finite-module patching

proof.text: For the enlarged list, the kernels of $P_B\twoheadrightarrow D$ and $P_{A'}\twoheadrightarrow C'$ are finitely generated ideals by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-surjection-kernel-fg]. A finite generating list for such an ideal is a finite relation list for the corresponding cyclic module. Hence $D$ is finitely presented as a $P_B$-module and $C'$ as a $P_{A'}$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Also $P$ is flat over $R$: as an $R$-module it is the direct sum of copies of $R$ indexed by monomials, and tensoring an injection with this module is the direct sum of that injection, which is injective coefficientwise [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The identifications and compatible module comparison from step 5 hold for the enlarged list as well.

source.place: Tag 08KQ, proof Ad (3), polynomial presentation; Tag 00R2, presentation independence

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-fp-module-fibre-product] with ambient algebra $S=P$ and modules $N=D$, $M'=C'$. Step 6 gives the two finite module presentations and flatness of $P/R$; their relative flatness is exactly the assumed flatness of $D/B$ and $C'/A'$. Thus $E=D\times_C C'$ is finitely presented as a $P$-module. Apply [lem-trf-finite-presentation-surjective-module-kernel] to the surjective $P$-linear evaluation $P\twoheadrightarrow E$. Its source is generated by $1$, so its kernel is finitely generated as a $P$-module, equivalently as an ideal of $P$. This yields a finite polynomial algebra presentation of $E/R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Combined with the flatness established in step 3, this proves the reverse direction of the second equivalence.

lean.statement: theorem flat_and_finitePresentation_iff {A A' B D C' : CommRingCat.{u}} (b : B ⟶ A) (q : A' ⟶ A) (hq : Function.Surjective q) (d : B ⟶ D) (c : A' ⟶ C') (φ : pushout b d ≅ pushout q c) (hφ : pushout.inl b d ≫ φ.hom = pushout.inl q c) : ((structureMap b q d c φ hφ).hom.Flat ↔ d.hom.Flat ∧ c.hom.Flat) ∧ (((structureMap b q d c φ hφ).hom.Flat ∧ (structureMap b q d c φ hφ).hom.FinitePresentation) ↔ (d.hom.Flat ∧ d.hom.FinitePresentation) ∧ (c.hom.Flat ∧ c.hom.FinitePresentation)) ∧ (∀ (L : CommRingCat.{u}) (ℓ : pullback b q ⟶ L), ℓ.hom.Flat → IsIso (reconstruction b q ℓ))
lean.note: Canonical categorical ring pullbacks and pushouts represent precisely the coordinatewise fibre products and tensor products of the node. The A-algebra isomorphism is a ring isomorphism with its A-structure compatibility equation. The quotient C prime / I C prime is represented canonically by its pushout along the surjection q.
